headline: Fuel margin strength drives sharp earnings growth
summary_short: Murphy USA's Q1 FY2026 net income more than doubled y/y to $136.3M (+156.2%) on revenue of $4,819M (+6.5% y/y), as total fuel contribution jumped 40.6% y/y to $403.9M on wider retail fuel margins.
summary_long: Revenue rose 6.5% y/y to $4,819M on a 3.3% higher average retail fuel price, 2.1% higher fuel volumes, and 5.0% higher merchandise sales. Total fuel contribution grew 40.6% y/y to $403.9M as retail fuel margin widened to 25.4 cpg from 23.7 cpg and fuel-supply/RINs contribution improved. Merchandise contribution rose 7.3% y/y on favorable mix and unit growth, led by 10.4% nicotine same-store-sales growth. Net income more than doubled to $136.3M (+156% y/y); diluted EPS rose to $7.28 (+177% y/y), aided by a 7.4% y/y drop in diluted shares from buybacks. Cash rose to $118.6M from $28.9M q/q on $320.0M of operating cash flow. FY2026 capex guided to $475-525M; $70.9M of shares repurchased in the quarter.

drivers.explanation: Higher total fuel and merchandise contribution combined with lower G&A expenses drove the earnings increase, partially offset by higher income taxes, store/opex, D&A, and interest expense.
Increase driven by a 3.3% rise in average retail fuel sales price, a 2.1% rise in fuel sales volumes, and a 5.0% rise in merchandise sales revenue.
Cost of sales grew 4.0% q/q on higher fuel cost, higher fuel volumes sold, and higher merchandise costs, outpacing revenue's q/q gain and compressing gross profit sequentially.
Diluted share count fell 7.4% y/y (20.204M to 18.708M) on buybacks, so EPS growth of 177% outpaced net income growth of 156% y/y.
Growth attributed to a $94.8M favorable swing in non-cash working capital, $83.1M higher net income, $10.7M higher deferred/noncurrent tax charges, and $3.9M higher depreciation.
Cash built q/q as $320.0M of operating cash flow outpaced $98.5M of investing outflows and $131.8M of financing outflows (buybacks, dividends, net debt repayment).
